pages.text: In chapter 4 you were already $(bold)spending$() Tokens on the closed-source cloud. The $(item)Cloud Compute Offload Node$() turns that around: rent out your own room's $(bold)spare computation$(), collect Tokens per tick, and close the loop where $(bold)open-source racks feed the closed-source API$().

pages.title: How to Fit It
pages.text: The offload node is a $(bold)part$(): mount it on a casing cell of a $(item)Liquid-Cooled Compute Rack$()'s wall, $(bold)at most one per rack$(). It needs two things:$(li)An $(item)API Credential Card$(): right-click a $(item)Satellite Ground Station$() controller to bind it, then insert the card here — the rental Tokens go to that card's account.$(li)$(#0E7490)A computation reception hatch$(): place one GT $(item)Computation Data Reception Hatch$() on the cabinet's rear $(bold)y=2$() $(item)Computer Casing$() cells and connect it to the transmission hatch with optical pipes.

pages.title: Pricing and Anti-Double-Spend
pages.text: Every tick the node $(bold)really requests$() the rack's spare CWU/t (capped at 64) and credits $(bold)actual rented CWU/t × (1.20 ÷ room PUE)$() as Tokens.$(br2)$(bold)A cooler room earns more$(): at PUE 1.20 the coefficient is 1.00, while a hotter room pays less for the same silicon.$(br2)$(bold)Strict anti-double-spend$(): the rented CWU/t is $(bold)actually deducted from that tick's budget$(). A Research Station or pretraining cluster asking in the same tick only ever gets the remainder — $(bold)one slice of computation is never both rented out and used locally$().

pages.title: When Payout Stops
pages.text: The node only bills when computation is $(bold)really rented and really delivered$(). Any of these stops the payout on that very tick:$(li)No credential card, or a card not bound to an account.$(li)No reception hatch on the frame, or a cut optical link.$(li)The rack itself at 0 CWU/t (no blades, no coolant, no power, unfixed maintenance, soft-mallet pause).$(li)A broken structure or an unloaded chunk.$(br2)The GUI names the exact reason, so it never looks busy while the ledger stays still.
